detail.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Make `cfg.dist` authoritative for distributed initialization and its training-loop consumers, preserving existing CLI behavior.

- Read backend, rank-local device selection, timeouts, process-group policies, flight-recorder settings, lazy initialization, JIT disabling, gradient alignment, and Torch FSDP2 selection from the run config.
- Register configuration before runtime services, once per startup path. Keep the existing duplicate-initialization guard.
- Keep `use_megatron_fsdp` only in `cfg.ddp`, removing its duplicate from `cfg.dist` without changing the CLI flag. Other DDP settings remain outside this migration.
- Keep distributed metadata consistent with the config without modifying legacy arguments.

## Issue tracking

Related to #3554 (training-loop consolidation).

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py`
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the formatting and lint checks on my PR

No kernel implementation changes; the kernel-determinism coverage check passes without an exemption. Scoped formatting/lint checks pass. All-files check-only pre-commit retains existing failures in untouched files.

### Validation

At `374faff62c15d8a00fdb85530c9675cb16a45467`, the scoped two-GPU suite passes 320 tests per rank, with four tests skipped because they require eight GPUs. The same baseline suite passes 299 tests per rank with the same skips.

Coverage includes config ownership with conflicting/deleted legacy fields, startup registration, fake process groups, flight-recorder precedence, FSDP2 wrapper selection, metadata, GPT/Hybrid/MiMo builders, checkpoint config serialization, FP8 delayed scaling, and local upcycling. FSDP2 wrapper-selection tests use controlled doubles; they are not end-to-end FSDP2 training validation.

### Code review

Independent full-diff review completed; findings addressed. This PR remains a draft.
